statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-123877 is a certificate validation bypass in Node.js https.Agent: getName() gives a request that omits ca and one that passes ca: [] the same Agent and TLS session-cache key, so a session authenticated under the default trust store can be resumed by a request whose own CA policy would reject the server. Node.js fixed it for 22.x in 22.23.5, released 2026-11-11: the November 2026 security release, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/november-2026-security-releases, lists 22.x among the affected release lines, and the 22.23.5 release notes, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.23.5, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/af6fbb6564 ('https: isolate Agent TLS policy keys'), which carries CVE-ID: CVE-2026-123877 and is in the v22.23.5 tag and not in v22.23.4; outside tests it changes lib/https.js. The CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-123877, lists every Node.js release before 22.23.5 as affected. The DHI nodejs-22 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from the upstream Node.js release tarball for their version, with no source patches. We checked the node binary, /usr/bin/node, in every published nodejs-22 package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 22.23.5-r0 reports v22.23.5 and carries the fix, while the earlier builds 22.22.0-r0, 22.22.1-r0, 22.22.2-r0, 22.22.2-r1, 22.22.3-r0, 22.23.0-r0, 22.23.1-r0, 22.23.2-r0, 22.23.3-r0, 22.23.4-r0, 22.23.4-r1 and 22.23.4-r2 report v22.22.0 through v22.23.4 and are affected. As a check, the node binary contains the getTlsOptionKey() helper this fix adds to lib/https.js in 22.23.5-r0 on both architectures, and does not in any earlier build. 22.23.5-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

CVE-2026-123877 is a Node.js certificate validation bypass: https.Agent gives a request that omits ca and one that passes ca: [] the same session-cache key, so a TLS session authenticated under the default trust store can be resumed by a request whose own CA policy would reject the server. Node.js fixed it for 24.x in 24.22.3, the 2026-11-11 security release (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/november-2026-security-releases), with commit 4f60230182, 'https: isolate Agent TLS policy keys' (https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/4f60230182), which carries this CVE id. Release notes: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.22.3. We read the node binary in every published DHI nodejs-24 package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64: 24.22.3-r0 is the first that reports Node.js v24.22.3 and contains the tlsPolicyObjectIds key map this commit adds to the embedded lib/https.js; 24.13.0-r0 through 24.22.2-r0 report Node.js 24.13.0 through 24.22.2 and lack it.
